name: Wakoucha

origin.regionNote: a national style — Kagoshima, Sayama, and others pack it too

categoryNote: English black tea is 红茶, named for the liquor. Chinese 黑茶 is the post-fermented class this atlas files as dark.
pluckStandard: one bud and two leaves, orthodox

processing.description: Japanese black tea as an orthodox make — wither, roll, oxidise, dry. Not CTC, not a smoked Tongmu tea.
Orthodox roll on small-leaf sinensis, often Benifuuki and its relatives.
Full enzymatic oxidation. The cup is 紅茶 in the Chinese sense: red liquor, black class in English.

profile.mouthfeel: lighter than Dian Hong, cleaner than cheap Assam

water.note: Just off the boil. A kyūsu is allowed; this is still a black tea.

storage: Airtight, away from sencha. Stable pantry tea.

qualityMarkers.test: whole twisted leaf you can unfurl; grains from a cutter are a different tea

compare.differentiator: Two island blacks. Ruby 18 is a Taiwanese hybrid with mint-cinnamon; wakoucha is Japanese sinensis, milder malt.

summary: Japanese orthodox black tea: 和紅茶, malt and honey from Benifuuki and its kin, a kyūsu that is allowed to pour red.
